about: The postcommunio of the formulary “Nativity of the Lord — Mass at Dawn” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: May the newness of the mystery of His birth ever renew us, O Lord, for His unique Nativity has banished humanity’s old condition. Through the same Jesus Christ, our Lord, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

a.g: May the newness of the mystery of His birth ever renew us, Lord
this same Jesus Christ, our Lord
who lives and reigns with You

ex.w007: In this reading the adjective qualifies “sacraménti” (w004): the mystery of Christ’s birth. “Huius” (w001) and “cuius” (w009) refer to Christ.

nt.w007: The form can also be a nominative agreeing with “nóvitas”. The spelling alone does not settle the case.

seg.tr: You have filled Your household, O Lord, with sacred gifts; always refresh us, we beseech You, through the intercession of her whose solemnity we celebrate. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

a.g: always, we beseech You, by her intercession
who lives and reigns with You
